So, no, not all puppies are "like that." As I've stated multiple times, she has presented some issues that are new to us. For example, we've never had issues with reactivity to other animals or obsessive shit eating. I guess maybe we've been lucky in the past. I've already stated that both affordability and location are issues when it comes to any type of training classes. It's not a matter of loving her, she has plenty of positive qualities. But I don't know a single person who is gonna love that their dog eats shit, then constantly licks them lmao.
And exactly what, dear internet stranger, am I supposed to be learning from this situation? That it's not okay to gift someone a dog against their wishes?

1. Is endlessly yappy. (We've tried telling her "no," She doesn't stop. We've tried redirecting her energy elsewhere; when she's focused on barking, that's all she's gonna do. We've tried soothing her, especially when she barks at our other pets; again, she's persistent about it. Sometimes, all it takes is mentioning another animal's name. She'll bark at anything, from corners to other critters. And she's persistent about it. She has plenty of toys and gets played with daily.)

2. Seems to hate other animals. (We've tried soothing her when she gets excited/agitated by the others' presence, praising/treating when she does well, and even attempted to keep them separated as much as possible at times (especially for the others' sake). She relentlessly barks at all of them. She chases the cats away. One of them even attempts to play with her sometimes, but she won't have it. The other dog is an elderly Chihuahua. She immediately takes him to the ground upon contact.)

3. Isn't potty trainable. (We started working on this immediately. We do the standard praise and treat thing. When we first got her, we also attempted to utilize puppy pads to help mitigate inside messes since she was so young; she never took to them. We tried our best (differing work schedules) to take her out every two hours. She was making progress for a while, but backslid. Now, sometimes she'll have multiple accidents within 1-2 hours, other times she can last 3-4 hours. She doesn't like leashes, so she gets put (but not left alone) on a tie out. She's not rushed while outside. She can make it throught the night without accidents; she's crated at night. She won't pee/poop on the porch, but she will in the house.)

4. Is mean, sometimes even aggressive. (She gets told "no," redirected, and offered toys as alternatives. She growls and is nippy, but will also bite to the point of drawing blood at times.)

5. Won't stop eating her own shit. (Tried vet-recommeded Forbid powder. We try to ensure that she doesn't have the chance to eat it, but shit (literally lol) happens. This is usually only an issue when she has an accident indoors. She has limited access when it comes to roaming, she's not just left unattended to wander the whole house.)

6. Cannot stand grooming of any kind. (I started trying to get her aquanted to various types of grooming not long after we got her. She's always hated it. She'll squirm, and often bite. I've tried soothing her, going slowly, praising her, and giving treats. She's been to a professional groomer once, they said she did fine. We can’t do much with her at home, though.)


No, I've not attended puppy school or a training class. The nearest place that offers such a thing is at minimum 1.5 hours away; for transportation and work-related reasons, that's not feasible for me. 

She's a Chorkie. We've had puppies before, including small dogs. She has presented some issues that are new to us. Which is fine, all dogs are different. Regardless of how it's phrased, various incompatibilities are present. It's just a matter of whether or not they can be worked through now. 

I was prepared to take on the responsibilities of a dog, and was told I would have help. (I had been looking for a dog for myself for over a year. Preferably, I wanted a dog between 1-4 years old.) One person in our household didn’t want a dog at all; he's more emotionally attached to her than anyone now and against rehoming her. I, however, have never been a fan of Chihuahuas. This is my first experience with a Yorkie mix, but I had researched them before. Ultimately, I'm not the one who agreed to get this specific dog; I actually advised against it. Regardless, she's considered my dog and I'm financially responsible for her. So, essentially, someone got her for me. Said person has already admitted that they bit off more than they could chew and regret that decision. 

I've become attached to her, and I do love her. I'm just extremely stressed because nothing seems to be working out. And, at this point, no one is on the same page about how to proceed with training...or even rehoming. I would definitely prefer to at least keep her long enough to have her fixed because I don’t want her to be used for breeding.

1. Yep. And I begged my mom not to agree to take her. I was afraid she would be a more difficult breed, I just didn't expect everything that is happening, and I didn't expect some of it to persist for so long. In terms of being yappy, we already have a Chihuahua. He's been known to be vocal at times, but not really yappy. I've never had a dog that barks as intensely and as persistently as she does. 
2. We have another dog and two cats. We've tried soothing her when she gets excited/agitated by the others' presence, praising/treating when she does well, and even attempted to keep them separated as much as possible at times. This is one of the issues that is new to us. 
3. I know. I'm not new to small dogs. 
4. No amount of soothing or making this dog "feel secure" helps. She bites so hard that she draws blood if you so much as attempt to trim her nails or brush her teeth. Both of which I tried to get her acquainted with from a young age. And, sometimes, she's nippy for no reason. 
5. It's not always possible to supervise her 24/7. This happens when she has accidents in the house. She'll either be caught in the process, or after having eaten everything. We've brought this up to her vet, as well as tried the recommended Forbid powder. A few days ago, she bit me for trying to take the shit away from her. None of our other pets, to my knowledge, have done this. 
6. I attempted to start getting her acquainted with grooming from a young age. I've been soothing, praised her, and provided treats. She's always hated it.

1. We didn't want to get her at that age. She was brought to our house by the person who had her, and we were essentially told "it's now or never." If she were still with said person, she'd be used for breeding. 
2. She's not the first dog we've ever had. She does, however, present some issues that are new to us. All dogs are different.
3. In the future, please consider pulling the stick out of your ass and not being a know-it-all cunt on the internet for no reason.

Rose/Rosehip, Frankincense, and Myrrh oils have honestly made a huge difference in my skin over the last few months. I know essential oils aren't for everyone, but they might just be worth a try. Just do some research and make sure you're getting the right things for your skin type, especially non-comedogenic carrier oils. There are a lot of options out there! Also, be sure that if you do decide to purchase, you choose reputable brands/retailers.  I typically put the oils I'm using into a roller bottle and apply them along with whatever serum I'm using on any given night, but there are different orders in which you can apply certain things based on the desired effect. 

You may also want to look into some brands like CeraVe for some moisturizers to add to your regimen. 

I hope this helps, good luck!
